items.title: Bertini: the general member of a family of divisors cut by a generating system on a smooth projective immersion is smooth
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the Bertini smoothness theorem in the form used by the Stacks Project: for a smooth X over k, a generating system of sections of an invertible sheaf L whose associated morphism to P(V) is an immersion, the general member H_v of the resulting family of divisors is smooth over k'. The proof sets up the universal divisor H_univ inside A^r_k times X, considers the singular locus Sigma of the projection q : H_univ -> A^r_k, argues that Sigma is closed because the smooth locus of a morphism is open, and reduces to proving that the image q(Sigma) is contained in a proper closed subset of A^r_k; since Sigma is of finite type over k it suffices to bound its dimension by r - 1 (proof lines 10966-10987 and the remainder of the proof to line 11057). H3: the dimension count for the singular locus of the universal family is a genuine research-level argument and is the heart of the theorem.
